evals.name: plain-init
evals.prompt: I just joined this project and I'm kind of lost. Can you create a code wiki that explains how the doit task manager works? Put it in the repo so the whole team can read it later.
evals.expected_output: An initialized, validated code wiki under docs/code-wiki/ with an index, at least one source-cited chapter page containing a Mermaid diagram, a single dated init log heading, and engine-written .code-wiki.json metadata. No temporary engine files remain.
expectations: A wiki is created under docs/code-wiki/ in the repo
docs/code-wiki/00-index.md exists
At least one numbered chapter page (e.g. 01_*.md) exists
docs/code-wiki/log.md contains exactly one new '## [YYYY-MM-DD] init | ...' heading
docs/code-wiki/.code-wiki.json metadata exists, proving finalize succeeded
Chapter pages cite real source paths (e.g. src/store.js, src/commands.js)
At least one Mermaid diagram appears in the wiki content
No temporary engine files remain (.code-wiki-run.json, .code-wiki-prompt.md)

evals.name: obsidian-deep-target
evals.prompt: Generate a code wiki for the src/ directory of this project. I use Obsidian, so make it Obsidian-friendly (wikilinks, frontmatter, callouts), and go deep — I really want to understand the internals.
evals.expected_output: An initialized wiki using Obsidian format targeted at src/, living under docs/code-wiki/src, with .obsidian scaffolding, deep-detail chapters using Obsidian conventions, source citations, a Mermaid diagram, one init log heading, and valid metadata.
expectations: The wiki targets the src/ directory and lives under docs/code-wiki/src
Obsidian scaffolding exists (.obsidian/app.json and a .gitignore ignoring .obsidian/)
Chapter pages use Obsidian conventions (wikilinks [[...]], YAML frontmatter, or > [!...] callouts)
Chapters reflect deep detail (substantial, internals-level explanation)
Chapter pages cite real source paths under src/
docs/code-wiki/src/log.md contains exactly one new init heading
docs/code-wiki/src/.code-wiki.json metadata exists (finalize succeeded)
No temporary engine files remain

evals.name: query-save-answer
evals.prompt: I'm trying to understand how doit avoids corrupting the tasks file if the process dies in the middle of a write. Can you figure it out from the code and add the explanation to the code wiki so it's saved for next time?
evals.expected_output: A query run against the existing wiki: a durable answer page filed under docs/code-wiki/answers/ that explains the atomic temp-file-then-rename write strategy citing src/store.js, exactly one new '## [date] query | ...' log heading, .code-wiki.json updated with action=query and the answer listed, and the existing wiki structure preserved. No temp files remain.
expectations: A durable answer page is filed under docs/code-wiki/answers/*.md
docs/code-wiki/log.md contains exactly one new '## [YYYY-MM-DD] query | ...' heading
docs/code-wiki/.code-wiki.json metadata was updated and lists the answer page (finalize query succeeded)
The answer cites the real source (src/store.js)
The answer explains the atomic write strategy (temp file + rename)
The existing wiki structure is preserved (index and chapters untouched by the query)
No temporary engine files remain

evals.name: update-for-clear-command
evals.prompt: Heads up — I just added a new `clear` command to doit (it wipes all tasks in one shot). Can you update the code wiki so it reflects the latest code?
evals.expected_output: An update run: the wiki refreshed to document the new clear command (and the store.clearAll change), exactly one new '## [date] update | ...' log heading, .code-wiki.json updated with action=update, existing structure preserved, and no temp files remaining.
expectations: docs/code-wiki/log.md contains exactly one new '## [YYYY-MM-DD] update | ...' heading
docs/code-wiki/.code-wiki.json metadata was updated (finalize update succeeded)
The wiki now documents the new `clear` command
The wiki reflects the store.js change (clearAll)
Existing structure is preserved (index and prior chapters still present)
Updated content cites real source paths (src/commands.js / src/store.js)
No temporary engine files remain
